In GSE, the system evaluates whether critical data sources are available before proceeding with complex reasoning. If any such source fails or returns empty data, the system halts and returns a null signal. This is modeled mathematically as a conditional function f(data) → {signal, null} where the condition checks for presence and validity of core inputs. For GSI, this translates into Bayesian updating where prior beliefs collapse to zero probability upon detection of invalid or missing data. The dualism between gating and enrichment sources ensures that only essential data affects final predictions, while supplementary data degrades gracefully. This structure prevents spurious conclusions from incomplete datasets and maintains robustness across varying data quality levels.
